production.note: US model years 2015-2017. Start: KBB, July 17, 2014, on the 2015 Mustang: "3.7-liter V6 will now carry a 300-horsepower rating". End: Motor Authority, January 17, 2017: "As part of the popular pony car's 2018 refresh, Ford is killing the entry level engine" and "If you want to get your hands on a V-6 Mustang, the 2017 coupe and convertible models are still on dealer lots." (source motorauthority-mustang-v6-dropped-2017).

body.note: Ford calls the coupe the Fastback. "the 2017 coupe and convertible models"; KBB 2015 prices a "V6 convertible" (source kbb-mustang-specs-2014).

aspiration.note: "3.7L V6: All-aluminum DOHC with Ti-VCT helps deliver ..."; no forced induction listed.

drivetrain.note: Rear-wheel-drive pony car; categorical, from Ford's description of the Mustang range.

transmission.note: Ford brochure, 3.7L V6: "6-speed manual or SelectShift automatic transmission"; KBB: "standard 6-speed manual transmission" and "optional 6-speed SelectShift automatic" (source kbb-mustang-specs-2014). The 10-speed automatic arrived for 2018, after the V6 was dropped.

powerHp.note: Quote (Ford's 2015 brochure): "3.7L Ti-VCT V6 300 hp @ 6,500 rpm 280 lb.-ft. of torque @ 4,000 rpm". Ford's release of 17 July 2014 (ford-mustang-release-2014): 'a standard 300-horsepower V6'. No rating change is reported for 2016-2017.

weightLb.note: 2015 V6 fastback with the standard 6-speed manual, base curb weight as released by Ford on 17 July 2014 and reported by two independent named-author outlets (weight step 2). Quote, Motor Authority (Nelson Ireson): "Mustang V-6: 3,526 lbs (manual), 3,530 lbs (automatic)". Quote, Torque News (Patrick Rall, source torquenews-mustang-weight-2014): "2015 Ford Mustang V6 Manual Transmission Fastback – 3,526". Ford's specification sheet itself could not be opened.
